sources.entry: JetBrains Compose Multiplatform - AI-assisted code completion for Kotlin multiplatform development.

summary.name: Compose Multiplatform
summary.one_liner: A declarative UI framework from JetBrains, powered by Kotlin Multiplatform, for building shared user interfaces across Android, iOS, desktop and web.
keywords: share ui between android and ios
build one ui for many platforms
use_cases: sharing UI code across Android and iOS apps
building a desktop app in Kotlin
building a web front end in Kotlin
sharing business logic between mobile platforms
building a taxi or e-commerce app with shared UI
developing audiobook or media apps with one codebase
summary.what_it_does: The page is a marketing page presenting Compose Multiplatform as a declarative framework for building shared UIs across Android, iOS, desktop and web, powered by Kotlin Multiplatform. It lists production apps that use it, including Feres (about 90% of UI shared), Markaz (100+ screens), Instabox (almost all UI shared on Android and iOS, with maps, camera and video kept native), and Fabuly (entire UI built with it since January 2024). Other named users include Physics Wallah, Wrike and BiliBili's Instant Message feature. The page gives no technical details about APIs, licensing or pricing. The listing also describes it as offering AI-assisted code completion for Kotlin multiplatform development, which the page itself does not mention.
notable: Built on Kotlin Multiplatform, sharing business logic as well as UI
Used in production by apps such as Feres, Markaz, Instabox, Wrike and Physics Wallah
Native maps, camera and video can be kept platform-specific while the rest of the UI is shared
caveats: The page is promotional and gives no pricing, licensing or technical limits
Platform support for desktop and web is named but not detailed on this page
